# A rebase runs both drivers, but never writes MERGE_HEAD and never calls the
# pre-commit finalize. What carries it: clean merges are sealed into %A by the
# driver, conflicted ones are reported by `sesam status` with rebase advice.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp main.txt $TMPDIR/main.txt
cp topic.txt $TMPDIR/topic.txt
cp resolved.txt $TMPDIR/resolved.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

# MAIN changes the secret.
cp $TMPDIR/main.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'main: change secret'

# TOPIC branches from before that and changes the same line.
exec git checkout -b topic HEAD~1
cp $TMPDIR/topic.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change secret'

# The drivers do run during a rebase: the log is merged semantically and the
# secret conflict lands as markers in the revealed (gitignored) file.
! exec git rebase master
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s; 1 conflict'
stderr 'the audit log was therefore semantically merged'

# The advice is rebase-specific: git never sets MERGE_HEAD here, so telling the
# user to run `git commit` (or to abort with `git merge --abort`) would be wrong.
stderr 'finish this rebase with .git rebase --continue.'
stderr 'start over with .git rebase --abort.'
! stderr 'git merge --abort'

grep '^<<<<<<< ' s
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'
stdout 'a rebase is in progress'
stdout 'git rebase --continue'

# Resolve the revealed file, then seal it: `git rebase --continue` runs no
# pre-commit hook, so nothing else will reseal the resolution for us.
cp $TMPDIR/resolved.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git -c core.editor=true rebase --continue

# The rebased commit carries the resolution, and the repo verifies.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'RESOLVED'
exec sesam status
stdout 'in sync'
! stdout 'in progress'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec git status --short
! stdout .

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- main.txt --
line one
MAIN
line three
-- topic.txt --
line one
TOPIC
line three
-- resolved.txt --
line one
RESOLVED
line three
